# Believers in the Absolute Mean a Right to Moral Holidays

But what does TRUE IN SO FAR FORTH mean in this case?[^1] To answer, we need only apply the pragmatic method.[^2] What do believers in the Absolute mean by saying that their belief affords them comfort?[^3] They mean that since in the Absolute finite evil is 'overruled' already, we may, therefore, whenever we wish, treat the temporal as if it were potentially the eternal, be sure that we can trust its outcome, and, without sin, dismiss our fear and drop the worry of our finite responsibility.[^4] In short, they mean that we have a right ever and anon to take a moral holiday, to let the world wag in its own way, feeling that its issues are in better hands than ours and are none of our business.[^5]

[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "What do believers in the Absolute mean by saying that their belief affords them comfort?"
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "They mean that since in the Absolute finite evil is 'overruled' already, we may, therefore, whenever we wish, treat the temporal as if it were potentially the eternal, be sure that we can trust its outcome, and, without sin, dismiss our fear and drop the worry of our finite responsibility."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "In short, they mean that we have a right ever and anon to take a moral holiday, to let the world wag in its own way, feeling that its issues are in better hands than ours and are none of our business."
